articles.title_zh: Rockstar Reveals Even More GTA 6 Screenshots as PS5 Release Draws Closer
articles.content_orig:
You're exactly two weeks away from playing GTA 6 .
To celebrate the fact, developer Rockstar has shared another batch of screenshots that are designed to showcase Vice City at its best, and the world beyond. Take a look below at a whopping 37 new screenshots:
GTA 6 comes to PS5 on 19th November 2026, but you can get your preload started from 10th November. Learn more in our GTA 6 Release Times and Preload guide , which is staying up to date as we near launch.
A lot of the images focus on protagonists Jason and Lucia, but we do catch glimpses of other characters, the nightlife, and more that'll be part of Leonida. What's your favourite picture? Share it in the comments below.
[source rockstargames.com ]
Liam grew up with a PlayStation controller in his hands and a love for Metal Gear Solid. Nowadays, he's found playing the latest and greatest PS5 games as well as supporting Derby County. That last detail is his downfall.
Ok yeah these look incredible and just remember ladies and gentlemen there are people out there that think this game will flop...
It's going to be so epic, can't wait!
@Oram77 that's hilarious, it's already been pre-ordered 5-10 million copies*
Me: I'm not going to look at those for spoiler reasons. Also me: Those were some great new screenshots.
Laura Branigan said it best in Vice City, you take my self-control.
Looks amazing. Can't wait, looking forward to Digital Foundry's video also
I still maintain that this looks exactly like GTA5.
@Oram77 There’s more chance of EA winning company of the year than this game flopping.
One of the people in the screenshots literally look like Kodak Black 👀
It looks good but I'll wait on the pc release. Especially now that the normal physical edition comes without the usual goodies (map etc). Plus I got too many games to play anyway.
@LifeGirl it looks nothing like gta 5! You might need specsavers
@LifeGirl I pity your optic nerves
The texture work and level of detail on every little thing is incredible.
If the texture on the bottom of the pool in that last one is simulated rather than a loaded texture...
Ain't no way this game runs at 60FPS...
Fingers still crossed for an actual disc edition (even if it's just a licence-on-a-disc) at some point after launch.
There is every indication the game will look incredible, but even with that in mind these are still bullshots.
Am I the only one that thinks we still have not seen nearly enough gameplay yet?
Looks alright doesn’t it? I guess it’ll do for now. Plus the soundtrack is ok too I suppose.
I expect to have a moderate amount of fun playing it, repeatedly, for hours, almost endlessly. Maybe.
Not too concerned with the frame rate either, as I’ll mainly have it static just overlooking the city whilst I wan … work.
@thechetearly totally unrelated to GTA 6, but excellent taste in music! That's a great album by The Chariot, only heard it recently.
As for GTA 6, it looks fun. I'm sure it will be. But I'm not feeling a real great hype. No doubt when it floods everywhere I look it will though, and I'll buy it soon after anyway.
I just want a return of San Andreas territory system really.
Pushsquare should do an article asking readers what they plan of doing when first booting the game up. I’ll probably spend the first few days just roaming the map and seeing what random things I come across. I certainly won’t be in any rush to finish the game. I made that mistake in gta5 thinking we’d get some dlc in the coming months/years.
I've started counting days and that was the worst decision to make in this situation. Suddenly, the march towards release has slowed to a crawl and the waiting has become excruciating. I'm a victim of hype.
@LifeGirl , you clearly have not played or seen GTA 5 next to GTA 6, or you need to visit an optician urgently.
I'm not intending to buy the game, but the screenshots are very impressive. My son absolutely loved GTA 5, so I imagine that he will get it, and as we game share on the Xbox I will have the opportunity to play it should I be persuaded to do so.
I do have to say, I wonder whether it will live up to the hype, and also whether it will get fantastic 10/10 reviews whilst at the same time numerous issues with the game are pointed out? I wonder whether professional reviewers will feel compelled to give the game 10/10s, or whether it will deserve them, and whether those same issues in another game would see it marked down? In other words, is the game too big to be critiqued properly?
I'm sure the game will be good, but will it be as good as we will be led to believe? I hope it is for the sake of all those that are really looking forward to it, but as someone on the outside of the hype, the excitement is kind of bewildering. To me, it's a bit like everyone raving about the latest Artic Monkeys album, when I just don't like their music and I cannot understand how anyone does... 😉
Laura Branigan, @GirlVersusGame ? Are you an old soul or just well versed on good music? I was there front of the queue to buy her first album when it released in 1982. I absolutely loved her...
All at a staggering beautiful 30fps. My time is on Zelda OOT.
@Oram77 game has already done $750 million in sales and it's not out yet. It can't literally bomb. But it can be a massive let down enough to shake the entire gaming foundation. I don't think it will be. But I still hold reservation for performance issues plaguing this game from when CD showed 48 minutes of Cyberpunk "gameplay" and we all know how that turned out at launch.
@AI-Generation I'll be playing both
As I'm still waiting for a 60fps mode for RDR2 before buying it, I'll probably buy and play GTA6 on a second hand PS6 Pro.
@Fiendish-Beaver Music is a kind of obsession and Vice City, along with many other games in the series helped to introduce me to so many good bands and musicians. Music is a big part of why I want to experience Six. I tend to prefer older music, movies and people. You definitely experienced the better timeline.
@Oram77 That’s fantastic, I’m not sure about GTA6 shall wait and see, as you know I have the 30fps hump 🤣
@Boxmonkey I bet that if you took a random landscape screenshot from both games and put them side by side you would not be able to tell the difference.
Can’t wait. It’s all ready. Ps5 pro, LG G5 and my Soundsystem. My only concern are the 30 fps, especially on an OLED. We will see how this turns out. Even it’s absolutely unrealistic: still having a glimpse of hope for any kind of 40 fps mode.
Grand theft auto i6 is going to be a instant and win game of the year. Word up son
Only 2 more weeks! Also getting my new ( and slightly bigger 😁 ) Oled next tuesday, so im ready for GTA6.
Yea hyped to play this now, lm away in switzerland sunday before it releases till the friday so that should make the time go faster 🤣. As soon as im back on friday it will be on all weekend and not moving only for food drink and toilet 🤣. Im glad we havent had too many trailers for it, can go in relativley blind to it.
@LifeGirl get real! There is a huge difference between gta5 and rdr2. I understand trying to be contrarian but this is taking it a little too far.

articles.title_orig: Why Sandisk Stock Keeps Going Down
articles.title_zh: Why Sandisk Stock Keeps Going Down
articles.content_orig:
For investors, it's not as much fun owning Sandisk ( SNDK -19.20% ) as it once was.
Shares of Sandisk, one of the world's leading producers of NAND flash memory for PCs, mobile devices, and -- increasingly -- artificial intelligence data centers , are still up 400% over the past 52 weeks. That's great for investors who got in on the ground floor. More recent Sandisk investors, however, have suffered terribly as Sandisk shares shed 36% of their value over just the last six trading days.
And as of 10 a.m. ET Thursday, Sandisk stock is down another 14.5%.
Image source: Getty Images.
Why is Sandisk stock still going down? Some blame Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT, which has been in the news a lot lately for boasting it invented a new "4F square" memory chip and plans to market it as high-bandwidth memory (HBM) for data centers.
Earlier today, CXMT announced it's received $1 billion in customer prepayments for its DRAM chips through the end of September, "a 15.7-fold increase from ... the end of 2025," according to DigiTimes.
NASDAQ · As of 1:58 PM ET 11/05/26
Should this worry Sandisk investors? Not necessarily.
Firstly, investors need to remember that although both CXMT and Sandisk make computer memory , CXMT focuses on DRAM, while Sandisk produces NAND flash memory exclusively. While competing tangentially in the "memory market," CXMT is not a direct competitor to Sandisk.
One area where the companies may compete in future is if Sandisk's invention of high-bandwidth flash (HBF) memory takes off as an alternative to HBM and CXMT succeeds in producing DRAM chips capable of being used as HBM. As DigiTimes reports, however, CXMT is struggling to transition its DRAM to HBM, and yield rates for its "next-generation HBM3E products" are only 20% to 30%.
If that's the best CXMT can do, Sandisk investors may have even less to worry about .

SpaceX ( SPCX ) and Tesla ( TSLA ) stocks extended declines on Thursday, each dropping roughly 9%. Shares of the Elon Musk-led companies were pounded after Democrats won control of the House and Senate this week, raising concerns over regulatory hurdles for data center buildouts in the US and merger aspirations between the two companies.
The Democratic win in Texas, where both SpaceX and Tesla are headquartered, is at the center of the concern. The state flipped blue at the gubernatorial level and saw the Senate seat won by James Talarico, with whom Musk got into fierce spats on social media leading up to the elections.
"We will believe a SpaceX/Tesla merger happens but now faces a much tougher regulatory roadmap to get this deal done in 2027 given this new political blue roadmap in DC/Texas," Yorkville's partner and managing director Dan Ives wrote on Thursday.
Elon Musk said on SpaceX's third quarter earnings call last month that he thinks merging the company with Tesla ( TSLA ) would be a good idea and revealed that both companies are exploring a potential deal.
Earlier this year, Musk also announced the launch of a Terafab, a massive semiconductor manufacturing complex in Texas that would supply SpaceX and Tesla.
Worries over a slowdown in data center build-outs also dampened shares of Texas-based SpaceX, which has increasingly leaned into AI compute as a revenue source.
Ives said while Big Tech and hyperscaler capex should still easily exceed $1 trillion in 2027, the growth rate into 2028 "will clearly moderate significantly as the data center buildout comes at a much slower pace given the political map, especially in the state of Texas."
On Wednesday, Goldman Sachs analysts also calculated, "Democratic wins at the state and local level are likely to lead to short-term data center moratoria, potentially affecting about 45% of planned US data center capacity expansion.

articles.title_orig: The US Midterm Elections: Views From China - The Diplomat
articles.title_zh: The US Midterm Elections: Views From China - The Diplomat
articles.content_orig:
The U.S. midterm elections on November 3 were closely watched around the world as a way to gauge public support for the polarizing administration of Donald Trump. The verdict is in: the opposition Democratic Party won big, taking control of both houses of Congress with majorities Democrats haven’t enjoyed in years. Several states elected Democratic senators and governors for the first time in decades – in some cases, nearly a century .
Officially, of course, China won’t comment on the results of the election. That, as Foreign Ministry spokesperson Mao Ning told reporters on November 4, is “a domestic affair” of the United States. “China stands ready to continue working with the U.S. to uphold and deliver on the important common understandings reached by the two heads of state,” Mao said.
In a speech delivered on election day, Xie Feng, China’s ambassador to the United States, said , “A confident and composed China is committed to the steady, sound, and sustainable development of China-U.S. relations… China’s policy toward the United States remains consistent and stable.”
The first news readouts from Xinhua, China’s state news agency, were also terse, although the points of information they chose to include were telling. In one early article , for example, Xinhua did not mention the historic nature of Democratic Party wins, but instead quoted Trump’s social media post that “I wasn’t on the Ballot and if I was, we would have won IN A LANDSLIDE!” The short, three-paragraph report also devoted the entire last paragraph to comments from a White House official, who predicted U.S. voters “will suffer from severe buyer’s remorse.”
Xinhua published a much longer analysis on November 4, highlighting four “unexpected” outcomes. This article delved into the massive scale of the Democratic victory, from the size of its new House majority to the flipping of Senate seats in traditionally safe Republican states like Texas, Iowa, Kansas, and South Carolina.
Rather than offering perspectives from Chinese analysts, Xinhua’s article extensively cited U.S. media, including this quote from the Wall Street Journal : “Rarely in American politics has a president traded away so much political support so quickly. The losses that Republicans suffered on Tuesday marked one of the most decisive repudiations of a president in modern history.”
Chinese state media had much less to say about the causes of the Republican defeat – again, Beijing’s official line being that this is an “internal affair” of the United States. However, Xinhua did cite the general thesis by U.S. analysts that economic dissatisfaction amid rising prices was the primary culprit. And those rising prices were exacerbated by the Trump administration’s decision to strike Iran. Xinhua published a whole article covering Vice President J.D. Vance’s post-election verdict that the war on Iran had cost the Republicans control of Congress.
One Xinhua report cited Iran’s Speaker of Parliament Mohammad Ghalibaf, who posted on X : “Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message.”
“What the Chinese public is most concerned about … is the impact of the U.S. midterm election results on the Iran war and Ukraine war,” Mu Chunshan, an independent political analysts based in Beijing, told The Diplomat via email. “They are less focused on the impact on China-U.S. relations. This is because Trump has consistently shown respect to China.”
If Democrats act to restrain Trump’s military operations in Iran, Mu said, it would be align “with China’s long-standing call for a peaceful resolution of the Iran nuclear issue.” He sees the election results as “conducive to China and other countries pushing for a negotiated resolution of the Iran nuclear issue and Strait [of Hormuz] security issues.”
That said, Chinese analysts are well aware of Congress’ limited control over foreign policy. In an pre-election analysis, South China Morning Post cited Zhao Zhijiang , a research assistant at the Beijing-based independent think tank Anbound, as predicting that “Diplomacy may become even more transactional. U.S. policy towards Russia, Iran, Europe and China could swing rapidly between heavy pressuring and partial bargaining.” In other words, China is bracing for impact as a notoriously mercurial leader feels increased political pressure at home.
Diao Daming, an international relations professor at Renmin University in Beijing, told SCMP Trump might become more “legacy-driven” in his pursuit of foreign policy.  “On the other hand, in areas he believes he can control or achieve results quickly, he may also take some risky actions,” Diao said.
With a Trump-Xi summit looming later this month, China will be one of the first to get a feel for how the midterm defeat impacts Trump’s foreign policy style. China is hosting the APEC Leaders’ Meeting from November 18-19, with Trump expected to attend. Beside yet another summit between Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping – the third in 2026 alone – there has been much discussion of other potential sideline meetings, including a possible China-Russia-U.S. trilateral.
China had its own reasons to be skeptical about hosting such a meeting . After the midterm outcomes, which will likely result in increased congressional support for Ukraine, there’s even less reason for Beijing to look positively on the prospects of a Putin-Trump-Xi meeting.
“At the APEC summit, if China, the US and Russia hold a trilateral summit, there is a high probability that the Ukraine war will not be discussed, because the midterm results make it harder for Trump to pressure Ukraine into accepting a ‘land-for-peace’ plan.” Mu said. “For China, discussing this is meaningless. Any peace plan must indeed fully take into account the views of Ukraine and Europe. This should be similar to the views of the new U.S. Congress.”
Also with the APEC summit in mind, Chinese policymakers will want to see if Trump is willing to strike a bargain to secure quick economic gains, given U.S. voter anger over the cost of living. There is also hope that a Democratic Congress would do more to push back on Trump’s use of tariffs – a tool that typically belongs to the legislative branch, not the executive, under the U.S. system of government.
“If the Democrats can restrain Trump’s impulses to China and other countries in the areas of tariffs and trade, that would be better for China-U.S. relations,” Mu said.
But few in China expect a Democratic-majority Congress to look too much different. “Structural contradictions exist in China-U.S. relations, and both the two parties share negative views on China, for example on national security or high-tech competition,” Mu noted. “These will not change in any particular way due to the outcome of the midterms.”
More broadly, Chinese analysts largely took the U.S. election results as evidence for already-held assumptions about a crumbling U.S. political system. Xinhua’s own original reporting , including on-the-street interviews with voters, portrayed a sense of pessimism and despair. Nearly all the quotes were from voters who expressed doubt that anything would change, regardless of who is in power. One sample: “I have no confidence in any politician, and I don’t think they will focus on what is right for us.”
That was a far cry from the palpable sense of optimism emanating from the Democratic Party as the election results rolled in. But it does fit nearly with China’s preferred thesis that the United States is locked into an irreversible decline.
And whatever Beijing may say about the election being the United States’ “domestic affair,” it will not be lost on Chinese leaders that an unpopular war far from home, and its economic consequences, resulted in severe political punishment for the ruling party. That will factor in to China’s ongoing calculations about what the Iran-U.S. war might imply about Americans’ appetite for intervention in a Taiwan crisis.

articles.title_zh: AppLovin stock soars after Q3 earnings, outlook beat
articles.content_orig:
Oops, something went wrong
Mobile app technology company AppLovin ( APP ) (NASDAQ:APP) announced better-than-expected revenue in Q3 2026, with revenue up 55.5% year on year to $2.18 billion. In addition, next quarter's revenue guidance ($2.38 billion at the midpoint) was surprisingly strong and 5.5% above analysts' consensus estimates. Its GAAP profit of $4.30 per share was 6.6% above analysts' consensus estimates.
For more on AppLovin, read our full research report .
AppLovin stock rose 18% before the bell on Thursday.
Revenue $2.18 billion vs analysts' consensus estimates of $2.07 billion, according to S&P (55.5% year-on-year growth, 5.4% beat)
EPS (GAAP) $4.30 vs analysts' consensus estimates of $4.03 (6.6% beat)
Adjusted EBITDA $1.84 billion vs analysts' consensus estimates of $1.73 billion (84.3% margin, 6.3% beat)
Revenue guidance $2.38 billion at the midpoint for Q4 2026, above analysts' consensus estimates of $2.25 billion
EBITDA guidance $2.01 billion at the midpoint for Q4 2026, above analysts' consensus estimates of $1.88 billion
Operating margin 78.2%, up from 76.8% in the same quarter last year
Free cash flow margin 64.9%, up from 45.2% in the previous quarter
Market capitalization $82.16 billion
A company's long-term revenue performance is one signal of its overall quality. Any business can have short-term success, but a top-tier one grows for years. AppLovin's revenue grew at a solid 24.8% compounded annual growth rate over the last five years. Its growth surpassed the average software company and shows its offerings resonate with customers.
Long-term growth is the most important, but within software, a half-decade historical view may miss new innovations or demand cycles. AppLovin's annualized revenue growth of 39.2% over the last two years is above its five-year trend, suggesting its demand was strong and recently accelerated.
This quarter, AppLovin reported strong year-on-year revenue growth of 55.5%, and its $2.18 billion of revenue beat Wall Street's consensus estimates by 5.4%. Management is guiding for a 43.6% year-on-year increase in revenue next quarter.
Looking further ahead, sell-side analysts expect revenue to grow 25.8% over the next 12 months, according to S&P, a deceleration versus the last two years. Despite the slowdown, this projection is strong and suggests the market expects success for its products and services.
The customer acquisition cost, or CAC, payback period measures the months a company needs to recoup the money spent on acquiring a new customer. This metric helps assess how quickly a business can break even on its sales and marketing investments.
AppLovin is highly efficient at acquiring new customers, and its CAC payback period was 1.2 months this quarter. The company's rapid recovery of its customer acquisition costs indicates it has a highly differentiated product offering and a strong brand reputation. These dynamics give AppLovin more resources to pursue new product initiatives while maintaining the flexibility to increase its sales and marketing investments.
AppLovin's outlook stood out in a quarter with clear positives: EBITDA guidance for next quarter came in well above analysts' consensus estimates, and revenue guidance also topped Wall Street's consensus. Shares soared 24.9% to $339.10 immediately after the results.
AppLovin had a positive quarter, but one earnings result doesn't necessarily make the stock a buy. Assessing whether it is a good investment requires considering its valuation and business quality, as well as what happened in the latest quarter. articles.title_zh: Stock Market Today: Rotation Away From AI Stocks Increases as Money Flows to AI Landlords - 24/7 Wall St.
articles.content_orig:
The S&P 500 looks flat before the bell, but a split is tearing through the market. After voters took aim at data centers, one group of AI winners is surging while the companies that supply them slide. The Fed speaks…
This post may contain links from our sponsors and affiliates, and Flywheel Publishing may receive compensation for actions taken through them.
The S&P 500 is headed for a near-flat start Thursday. As of about 8:20 a.m. ET, funds that track the index were up 0.1% before the bell. Under that calm number, the S&P 500 is splitting in two. Hyperscalers and Apple ( NASDAQ:AAPL | AAPL Price Prediction ) are adding to Wednesday’s post-election rally, while chipmakers are falling on concerns that voters just made AI data centers harder to build. The biggest scheduled event of the day is the Federal Reserve’s policy statement at 2 p.m. ET.
On Tuesday, Democrats flipped both the House and Senate. Voters also sided against AI data centers in 40 of 41 local ballot measures, according to CNBC . Investors took that to mean the AI expansion will be slower and more expensive. That outcome helps the companies that already own data centers and hurts the ones selling them chips.
Amazon ( NASDAQ:AMZN ) jumped 8% Wednesday and is up another 2% premarket. Apple rose nearly 7% Wednesday and is adding 1%.
Apple trades near $354. Because the Dow is price-weighted, a stock with a share price that high has extra pull on the index. This is why the Dow leads this morning.
NVIDIA ( NASDAQ:NVDA ) is down 2% premarket, adding to an 18% drop over the past month. Intel ( NASDAQ:INTC ) is off 3% and has lost 51% in a month.
The leveraged Direxion Daily Semiconductor Bull 3X ETF ( NYSEARCA:SOXL ) is indicated down 11%. The fund resets every day to deliver triple the chip index’s move, so losses pile up fast when chips keep falling.
While the Dow rises, the Nasdaq-100 proxy is falling. That gap shows money moving away from chip suppliers and toward blue chips and companies that already own AI capacity (we featured seven suppliers behind the data center expansion, from power to cooling, in a free report you can grab here ). Needham analyst Laura Martin summed it up: “Hyperscalers are AI incumbents.” Siebert Financial’s Mark Malek pointed to where the risk lies: “The most vulnerable AI companies are the borrowers, not necessarily the biggest spenders.”
Wall Street’s concerns gauge, the VIX, is almost 21. That puts it in elevated territory, up 3 points from a week earlier. The 10-year Treasury yield is just under 5%, which keeps borrowing costs high for the rate-sensitive small caps in the Russell 2000.
The top of the Fed’s target range is 4% going into today’s announcement. Any hint about future rate cuts will likely move small caps and high-valuation tech the most. Through the session, keep an eye on whether chip stocks steady as investors work out how far state-level limits on data centers can actually reach.

articles.title_orig: James Carville Tells Trump His Misery Is Only Just Beginning
articles.title_zh: James Carville Tells Trump His Misery Is Only Just Beginning
articles.content_orig:
Veteran Democratic strategist James Carville predicted that President Donald Trumpâs life is going to get far worse after Democrats seized control of Congress in their midterm landslide.
âIf you listen to me, President Trump, youâre probably not, but somebody is. Itâs going to get worse. Youâre going to get more depressed,â said Carville, in an appearance Wednesday on the Politicon podcast with Al Hunt.
In the interview, Carville urged the new Democratic crop of lawmakers elected to House and Senate majorities to send a clear anti-corruption message, for example, by banning stock trading by members of Congress. âCorruption is for good reason becom[ing] front and center here,â he said.
James Talarico supporters celebrate on an historic night in Texas.
Polls ahead of the midterms showed government corruption was among votersâ key concerns, with 89 percent of respondents in a September Gallup poll saying they believed it was widespread.
Despite Trump holding veto power over any new legislation passed by the Democratic Congress, Carville said the party could do real damage to the president by putting the issue firmly in the spotlight.
By clicking â SUBSCRIBE â you agree to our Terms of Use and Privacy Policy .
âYou can have intensive, rigorous investigations, and at the same time, pass legislation [that] may not be enacted in the law. You then set an agenda,â he said.
Carville pointed to âhow much they [Democrats] can do in terms of bringing to light all of the corruption thatâs taken place, and I think theyâre going to do that.â
Carville also said the results had exposed divisions in the GOP, with Vice President JD Vance in a post on X Wednesda y appearing to criticize his bossâs election strategy and the war with Iran that proved another key factor in the Republican defeat.
âI think the tension with Vance in the White House is going to get greater, and it was a bad night for Republicans,â said Carville.
Vance is at his core a skeptic of U.S. military intervention in the Middle East.
Carville masterminded President Bill Clintonâs election victories in the 1990s, and has long been an adamant critic of Donald Trump.
On the eve of the midterms, he predicted a Republican wipeout. In an appearance on MS NOW , he said he believed the economy and allegations of corruption against Trump and his inner circle would decide the vote.
âI think people have tied corruption to the economy, so I want to be very clear. Corruption is a challenge, and every election is about the economy. It always has been. But I think the corruption issue is really kind of center stage,â he said.
